summary.one_liner: Agent-C is an ultra-lightweight AI agent written in C that talks to the OpenRouter API and can run shell commands as tool calls.
summary.what_it_does: The agent sends chat messages to OpenRouter with a single `sh` tool definition using the OpenAI-compatible tools API. Responses stream to the terminal token by token via SSE. When the model returns tool calls, the agent executes the command, returns the output to the model, and gets a follow-up reply, up to 5 tool calls per turn. It keeps a sliding window of 20 messages, including tool call history, as conversation memory. The README says it uses native TLS (macOS SecureTransport) instead of curl or libssl, and the build targets a single source file, agent.c, packed into a small binary.
use_cases: run an AI assistant from the terminal
let an LLM execute shell commands
chat with OpenRouter models from C
minimal footprint AI agent on macOS or Linux
how_to_run: make macos  # macOS build with LZMA compression
make linux  # Linux build with UPX compression
notable: Zero dependencies: no curl or libssl, native TLS on macOS
Single-file implementation (agent.c) with a roughly 4KB binary claim
OpenAI-compatible tools API used for shell command execution
Streaming output printed as tokens arrive
Sliding window conversation memory of 20 messages
caveats: README names macOS and Linux only; TLS path is described for macOS SecureTransport
Requires an OpenRouter API key via OR_KEY
Executes model-requested shell commands, so it runs with the user's permissions
